Urim and Thummim
OOR-im and THUM-im
n. phrase (Hebrew)
Hebrew ’ūrīm (“lights”) and tummīm (“completeness, perfections”); the names of the sacred objects placed in the high priest’s breastplate of judgment, by which the LORD revealed His will to His people on appointed occasions.

See also: Urim and Thummim

📖 Biblical Definition

The Urim and Thummim were sacred objects placed inside the breastplate of judgment of the high priest, by which the LORD revealed His will to His people on appointed occasions in the Old Testament. The Hebrew words mean approximately lights and perfections (or completenesses). Their precise physical nature is not described in Scripture; they appear suddenly in Exodus 28:30 without prior introduction (and thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goeth in before the LORD: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the LORD continually), suggesting that they were familiar to Moses and the original readers though obscure to later interpreters. Several structural features mark the doctrine. First, they were given to the high priest, not to the lay Israelite—the channel of revelation was through the appointed priestly office. Second, they were within the breastplate of judgment, which was on the high priest’s heart (Ex 28:29-30)—the place of judgment-decision-making, brought before the LORD. Third, they functioned in cases of national or covenantal significance where the LORD’s direct guidance was sought. The biblical narrative shows Urim-and-Thummim consultations: Numbers 27:21 (Joshua’s succession to Moses, with the judgment of Urim before the LORD appointed as the means of inquiry); Joshua 7 (the search for the cause of defeat at Ai, presumably by sacred lot); Judges 1:1-2; 20:18-28 (Israel inquires of the LORD before going up to battle); 1 Samuel 14:36-42 (Saul’s inquiry with the priest before the battle with the Philistines); 1 Samuel 23:9-12; 30:7-8 (David inquires through the ephod with the priest Abiathar); 2 Samuel 21:1 (David inquires of the LORD concerning the famine). The Urim and Thummim therefore served as a specific divinely-appointed means of guidance for moments of national or military or covenantal decision in the OT period. The disappearance of the Urim-and-Thummim is noted post-exilically: Ezra 2:63 and Nehemiah 7:65 mention that certain priests who could not prove their genealogical descent were forbidden to eat of the most holy things till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim—implying that the Urim and Thummim were no longer functioning in the post-exilic period. The reason for the cessation is not explicitly given in Scripture; the broader pattern is that the Old Covenant means of revelation gave way to the more complete revelation in Christ. Hebrews 1:1-2: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son. The New Covenant believer therefore does not seek guidance through Urim-and-Thummim or similar sacred-lot mechanisms; he has the more complete revelation of the Son and the indwelling Spirit applying Scripture to his particular providences.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines URIM AND THUMMIM as Hebrew terms for “lights and perfections”; the sacred objects in the high priest’s breastplate by which divine guidance was sought in the Old Testament period; their nature is not described in Scripture, and their function ceased in the post-exilic era.

expand to see more

URIM, n. — A Hebrew word denoting lights, used to denote a part of the sacred ornaments of the priests under the Mosaic law. Urim was inserted in the breastplate of judgment which was worn by the high priest.

THUMMIM, n. — A Hebrew word denoting perfection; in scripture, paired with Urim as the sacred objects in the high priest’s breastplate by which divine guidance was sought.

📖 Key Scripture

Exodus 28:30 — "And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goeth in before the LORD: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the LORD continually."

Numbers 27:21 — "And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation."

Ezra 2:63 — "And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim."

Hebrews 1:1-2 — "God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The Urim-and-Thummim doctrine is corrupted by the speculative-method tradition that has, especially in some Christian guidance-and-decision-making books, attempted to reconstruct Urim-and-Thummim-style sacred-lot mechanisms for contemporary use—against the apostolic pattern that the New Covenant believer is guided by the Spirit’s application of the completed Scripture, not by sacred-lot or divinatory mechanisms.

expand to see more

The speculative-method tradition has, especially in popular Christian guidance literature, attempted to reconstruct Urim-and-Thummim-style sacred-lot mechanisms for contemporary use: fleecing (after Gideon’s fleece in Judges 6, which was itself an exceptional sign and not a generalizable method); randomly opening the Bible to find a verse for direction; subjective impressions interpreted as direct divine speech; various forms of sacred-lot casting. Scripture does not authorize any of these as ordinary means of New Covenant guidance. The Urim and Thummim were a specific OT-administration means tied to the high priest’s office, which ceased in the post-exilic period and have no NT counterpart. The apostolic pattern of guidance is different: Scripture as the foundational and sufficient revelation, the Spirit’s ongoing illumination of Scripture, the providential opening and closing of doors, the counsel of mature believers, the application of wisdom drawn from the whole of Scripture to the particular providence. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path (Ps 119:105) is the controlling NT-applied pattern, not Urim-and-Thummim-style direct oracular consultation.

The pastoral application is therefore important. The New Covenant believer seeking guidance is not abandoned to subjective impression or sacred-lot speculation; he has more than the OT saint had, not less. He has the complete Scripture, applied by the indwelling Spirit, in the company of the church, under providence governed by the same God who has spoken His word. The disciplined NT pattern of guidance includes: prayer for wisdom (James 1:5); the search of Scripture for principles that apply to the present providence; the counsel of mature saints and elders; the patient waiting under the providence God has placed one in; the active obedience to the clear commands of Scripture while specific decisions are pending; the willingness to be redirected by providential opening and closing of doors. This is more substantial than Urim-and-Thummim ever was, because the revelation in Christ is fuller than the revelation given to Moses. The recovery is the recovery of confidence in the NT pattern: Scripture, Spirit, providence, counsel—the ordinary means by which the Lord guides His people through every season of decision in the present age.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ’ūrīm (lights) and tummīm (completenesses); the sacred objects in the high priest’s breastplate of judgment by which the LORD revealed His will in appointed OT decisions; ceased in the post-exilic period; superseded under the New Covenant by the Spirit’s application of the completed Scripture.

expand to see more

Hebrew ’ūrīm (H224) — lights (paired with Thummim; 7 OT uses).

Hebrew tummīm (H8550) — perfections, completenesses (paired with Urim).

Hebrew chōshen ha-mishpāt — breastplate of judgment (the housing of the Urim and Thummim).

Greek klēros (G2819) — lot (the cousin term; the NT use in Acts 1:26 of casting lots for Matthias is the last canonically-recorded use of the sacred-lot mechanism, prior to Pentecost).

Usage

"The judgment of Urim before the LORD—the OT-administration means of seeking divine guidance through the high priest’s appointed instruments."

"The Urim and Thummim ceased in the post-exilic period; the post-Pentecost NT pattern is guidance through Scripture applied by the Spirit, in the company of the church, under providence."

"Speculative attempts to reconstruct Urim-and-Thummim mechanisms for contemporary use miss the apostolic pattern; the NT believer has more than the OT saint had—completed Scripture, indwelling Spirit, gathered church, governing providence."
